significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish a form-(iii) predictive coupling—“DiversionScore predicts per-example recall failure”—backed by the form-(ii) mechanism that distractor-directed retrieval attention causes a stored, mid-layer-decodable fact not to surface and that “attention re-focusing” reverses the failure. This fixes expectations for how failure probability varies with measurable attention diversion and distractor type, while separating the behavioral phenomenon of context-induced recall loss from a mechanistic routing-versus-storage explanation relevant to factual-recall accounts such as Geva et al. (2023) and the distraction effects documented by Shi et al. (2023). True and false are distinguishable: a negative result would rule out attention diversion as the proposed common mediator—especially if facts remain decodable—although it would not by itself identify the alternative mechanism. Topic substitution lowers the assessment from the level warranted by knowledge retrieval generally, but not below the topic median: the specific diversion-to-failure coupling, storage invariance, and causal repair constrain substantially more than the obvious hypothesis that query context affects retrieval.

reach.justification: The transferable handles named by the claim are “DiversionScore,” an example-level predictor, and the training-free “attention re-focusing” intervention; the former is weakly ex ante because it is available at the answer position before the answer token is emitted, while the latter can alter that emission, though both depend on identifying retrieval heads and distractor spans. After per-model re-extraction, the claimed relation still predicts that greater distractor attention means greater failure risk and that lexical-overlap distractors are most hijacking, rather than merely supplying an open-ended procedure for finding an unrelated direction. The hypothesis is framed across distractor classes and model families, and could support researchers or auditors who gate or repair context-sensitive factual answers, but practical uptake is limited because reliable distractor-span detection is only an “unsupervised variant” and the main conclusion concerns controlled irrelevant contexts. Under topic substitution, generic knowledge-retrieval importance would not earn this score; the above-median reach comes specifically from the named predictor, pre-emission intervention window, and relation expected to survive recalibration.
